title: Intershift Handoff Playbook & Weekly Ops Recap - 2026-12-01
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the week-of-2026-11-25 intershift handoff observations, a short incidents digest, SLO health snapshot, and an updated lightweight playbook for handoffs between night/day/relay shifts. The goal is to reduce context loss between shifts and cut time-to-remediation for common alerts.

Summary (one line):
- Slight uptick in prefix cache contention and two P1 blips tied to infra autoscaler thrash; handoff friction identified in partial runbook access and stale alert-snooze notes.

Sections:
1) Incident highlights (this week)
- Incident SRE-4821 (2026-11-27 02:13 UTC) — P1 latency spike across hosted-api-frontend cluster. Symptoms: 95th latency for generation endpoints rose from 220ms to 1.3s for ~18 minutes. Root-cause: thundering websocket reconnects + autoscaler reacting to short-lived queue growth causing pod churn. Mitigation: disabled aggressive scale-down policy, warmed extra nodes from Dedicated pool, enabled temporary sticky connection routing to reduce reconnect storms. Follow-ups: update autoscaler smoothing window (action 1), add a reconnect cooldown in gateway (action 2).
- Incident SRE-4837 (2026-11-29 16:40 UTC) — KV-cache eviction jitter on quantized-serve nodes. Symptoms: small but recurring error spike (500s) at mid-throughput. Root-cause: memory accounting mismatch in quantized allocator under mixed-precision load. Mitigation: rolled back recent allocator tweak, reloaded stable allocator, raised cache.soft_limit by 10%. Follow-ups: add allocator regression test to CI (action 3), create telemetry dashboard for per-node allocator pressure (action 4).
- Customer-facing outage (brief, non-P1) on 2026-11-30 09:05 PST: a Dedicated tenant routing rule expired during a config deployment. Impact: <2% of tenant requests returned 503 for ~7 minutes. Remediated by reapplying validated route config. Action: extend deployment gating for routing rule checks (action 5).

2) SLO snapshot (end of week):
- Text-generation P99 latency SLO (<= 1200ms): currently 98.7% compliance week-to-date (target 99%), trending up due to incident SRE-4821.
- API availability SLO (>= 99.95% monthly): current 99.96% month-to-date.
- Embeddings throughput SLO (sustained 2k rps for large-vec-v1): 99.9% uptime on reserved pools.
Notes: We dropped 0.3% from generation P99 from baseline; expected to recover after autoscaler smoothing change.

3) On-call handoff pain points observed (qualitative):
- Handoff notes inconsistent: some shifts list only the incident number without mitigation steps or links to runbook sections.
- Runbook discoverability: night-shift engineers often lack quick links to the exact subsection (e.g., gateway reconnect mitigation) and end up re-triaging.
- Alert noisiness: certain low-entropy alerts (cache-warm failures) are still firing during deployments, creating background noise during handoffs.
- Pager fatigue correlation: the same engineer often gets pages on consecutive shifts due to rotation overlaps.

4) Intershift handoff playbook (concise, to be pinned in Slack channel and runbook):
- Before shift end (15–30 min):
  * Add an entry to the oncall-handoff doc with: incident numbers, short status, mitigation applied, and explicit next steps. Use the template: "INC-ID — summary — mitigated: yes/no — mitigation details link: <url> — followups: <JIRA keys> — owner until next shift: <name>".
  * Snapshot current SLO dashboard and paste link (SRE clipboard command).
  * Ensure runbook links in the doc are permalinks (not to top-level runbook index).
- Handoff reception (first 10 min):
  * New shift ack the handoff doc and post one-line readback in #sre-handovers.
  * Confirm escalation contacts for active incidents (who will be the primary escalation path for network/infra/app layers).
- Severe incident escalation (P1/P0):
  * Active-in-progress: if a P1 intersects the shift boundary, the oncoming shift must join the bridge within 5 minutes of handoff post.
  * Bridge ownership: outgoing owner stays as bridge co-owner for 15 minutes unless explicitly passed.
- Post-handoff cleanup (first 60 min):
  * Update runbook with any temporary mitigations taken.
  * If runbook steps differed from documented flow, create a short note and tag runbook-owner for triage.

5) Immediate action items (owners and ETA):
- Action 1: Increase autoscaler smoothing window default from 30s to 90s on hosted-api (owner: Michael Chen, ETA: 2026-12-03).
- Action 2: Add gateway reconnect cooldown (owner: Rosa Alvarez, ETA: 2026-12-07).
- Action 3: Add allocator regression test to CI (owner: Devon Park, ETA: 2026-12-10).
- Action 4: Build allocator pressure dashboard (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-12-08).
- Action 5: Add routing-rule liveness check to deployment pipeline (owner: Platform Eng oncall, ETA: 2026-12-06).

6) Runbook and tooling updates to be made this sprint:
- Create a dedicated "handoff-template" snippet in the runbook repo so oncall scribes can quickly paste structured notes.
- Add a lightweight runbook entry: "Gateway reconnect storms" with TL;DR and mitigation commands.
- Add per-alert suggested snooze durations to reduce handoff noise.

7) Observations for the next rotation and experiments to try:
- Pilot a 10-minute synchronous overlap for critical shifts next week (test: Dec 6–10) where outgoing and incoming oncall do a short pairing session to review active incidents. Measure handoff completeness via a quick checklist.
- Try automated handoff digest: a small Lambda that compiles all open incidents, linked runbook sections, and SLO snapshot and posts to #sre-handovers at shift boundary (owner: DevRel infra); prototype by 2026-12-09.

8) Retro notes (what went well / what should change):
- Went well: quick rollback path for allocator tweak, good cross-team responsiveness on Dedicated routing fix.
- Should change: reduce manual runbook link hunting; standardize the handoff template; reduce pager duplication during rotation transitions.

9) Meeting / sync schedule and who to invite:
- Handoff retro sync: 2026-12-03 14:00 UTC — invite: SRE rotation leads, platform eng, gateway owners, product ops.
- Runbook grooming: 2026-12-07 10:00 UTC — invite: runbook-owners, CI owners, oncall leads.

Appendix: useful links and references
- SLO dashboard (perm): https://dash.redwood.ai/slo/generation-p99
- Incident SRE-4821 timeline: https://incident.redwood.ai/4821
- Runbook: Gateway reconnect storms: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/gateway-reconnects

Notes to reviewers:
- Please comment inline on the proposed autoscaler smoothing change if you have throughput-sensitive workloads that would be affected.
- If you own any of the action items above and need to adjust ETA, update this doc and ping the SRE rotation leads.
